about: Born, Not Made, quilted shell variant (22 Nov 2026). Frame: x toward the mouth, y port, z up, meters; origin on the docking plane, on the inner floor.

dex.t: Rotrics DexArm specification page (opened 22 Nov 2026): payload 500 g max (400 g in the Teach and Pneumatic section), reach 380 mm (Teach and Pneumatic section), weight 2.4 kg, repeatability 0.05 mm, base plus or minus 110, joint 1 0 to 110, joint 2 0 to 85 degrees

stages.name: Dock in the water
stages.text: Water in the tank and gel in both parts from the first frame. The tail slides forward and docks from behind, its gel face against the gel face of the head; the last 10 mm slowly. Nine magnets in the tail face pull the steel disks in the cuff of the quilted head.

stages.name: Unfold, top up
stages.text: The arm unfolds. The gel is already in (5.39 L); the line on the arm only tops up the 42 mL that left with the last newborn.

stages.name: Kit
stages.text: The electromagnet picks the electronics kit once, from its place in the tail, and carries the kit through the gel to the print seat, before any printing.

stages.name: Tool change
stages.text: One tool change in the tail: holder off, print needle on (Rotrics quick release). The needle travels in the gel to the print.

stages.name: Print
stages.text: The DexArm prints the next head folded flat around its kit: 632 m of bead, 1.17 L of Dragon Skin 30.

stages.name: Cure, change
stages.text: Cure, and the second tool change: print needle off, holder on.

stages.name: Birth a: the keel opens the folds
stages.text: The ball needle in the valve; the keel fills first and straightens the three lengthwise folds; the mouth end slides over the lip, cupped, on the keel.

stages.name: Birth b: push while inflating
stages.text: The holder pushes the rim at 2 mm per second; air is fed in steps matched to the advance, so each section opens only outside the lip.

stages.name: Birth c: the crank, rim past the lip
stages.text: The holder takes the valve again with its folding crank and pushes the rim 20 mm past the lip; only then the rim zone fills.

stages.name: Birth d: off the lip
stages.text: The needle leaves; the rear slides off the lip and the newborn settles on the tank floor in front of the mouth.

stages.name: The newborn, free
stages.text: The newborn lies free in front of the mouth. It does not move by itself; the tail comes to it.

stages.name: Relay: back away
stages.text: The tail backs the docked parent body away from the newborn and toward the port wall.

stages.name: Relay: tilt release
stages.text: Tilt release of the dock magnets on their hinged tabs; the old head stays against the port side.

stages.name: Relay: the lane
stages.text: The tail goes round the old head and comes in behind the newborn.

stages.name: Relay: dock
stages.text: The tail docks on the rim of the newborn.

stages.name: Relay: gel
stages.text: Gel into the newborn, then its lip circuit at 9 kPa.

stages.name: Next cycle
stages.text: The first frame of the next cycle: the newborn is the head; the tail needs a new pair of tile sets.

notes: The tank is full and the gel is in from the start: each part holds its own gel at the open docking face, level with the water. The tail slides forward along the floor and docks from behind; the two gel faces meet and the water between them is squeezed out. Nine magnets in the tail face pull the steel disks in the cuff of the quilted head; the cuff seals on the cord seat.
The arm unfolds out of the tail, over the gel. The base does not move.
The line on the arm tops up the gel that left with the last newborn (42 mL); no filling, the gel stays from birth to birth.
The bare arm folds back into the tail.
The bare arm turns to the holder: an electromagnet and a ball needle on a saddle beside the arm.
The quick release slides onto the holder and clicks.
The holder leaves its saddle sideways, its needle in the gel, and turns to the kit, which waits in the gel in front of the arm.
The magnet lands on the steel disk of the kit.
Magnet on: the magnet holds tile set 1 by its steel disk.
Tile set 1 is carried forward through the gel, across the seam, to the floor of its pockets.
The tiles go down onto the gel floor, square to the body, where the print will lay their pockets over them.
Magnet off: the tiles stay, held by the gel; the holder lifts clear.
The holder goes back to the magazine; the second set has slid into the pick pocket on its rails.
The magnet lands on the steel disk of the second set.
Magnet on: the magnet holds tile set 2 by its steel disk.
Tile set 2 is carried forward through the gel, across the seam, to the floor of its pockets.
Tool change in the tail: the holder comes back through the gel.
The holder slides sideways onto its saddle.
The pin on the saddle presses the release; the module stays.
The bare arm turns to the print needle on the other side.
The quick release clicks onto the print needle.
The needle leaves its saddle sideways, its tip in the gel.
The needle moves forward through the gel, across the seam, to the print.
The next head is printed folded flat, 18 layers, around its kit, layer by layer, in Dragon Skin 30.
The silicone cures in the gel (Dragon Skin 30: 16 hours at room temperature, Smooth-On bulletin). The print needle goes back over the print to its saddle in the tail.
The holder is back on the arm: the ball needle beside the magnet now carries the air.
Birth: the holder goes to the valve at the rim of the next head, at the rear of the folded pack.

a. The ball needle is in the valve. The keel (two rows of 16 mm tubes) fills first, to 23 kPa: it straightens the three lengthwise folds, and the mouth end slides up the chin and over the lower lip, cupped, lying on the keel.

b. Push while inflating: the holder pushes the rim; the six serpentines are fed from the mouth end in steps matched to the advance (8 mL of air per mm), so the inflation front stays 15 mm past the lip; each section opens across only outside and lies on the water and the tank floor. Inside and on the lip the strip stays flat, cupped.
c. The ball needle leaves the valve (the ball closes it); the holder backs off over the empty floor behind the rim.
c. The crank swings down: 120 mm forward of the tool axis, a short needle at its end.
c. The crank needle goes to the valve from above.
c. The crank needle enters the valve.
c. The crank pushes the rim over the lip and 20 mm past its edge. The rim zone stays empty: open, the rim (314 mm wide) would lock in the 213 mm mouth.
c. The rim is past the lip: the last zone, at the rim, fills now, outside.
d. The newborn lies nose down: the rear of the keel on the lip edge, the front on the tank floor. A last push of 4 mm takes the keel end off the edge.
d. The needle leaves; the ball valve closes.

d. The rear slides off the lip edge and down into the water; the newborn settles level in front of the mouth, its floor on the tank floor (the air in its lower cells does not carry it: 10.7 N rest on the floor; its own lip circuit is filled with gel at 9 kPa only when the tail docks to it).
The newborn lies free in front of the mouth: a quilted head of the same form as the parent, its gel film in its cells. The holder draws back into the head.
The newborn, free, on the tank floor. It does not move by itself.
The crank folds up along the stem; the holder goes back into the tail.
The holder is parked on its saddle.
The bare arm folds into the tail.
The tail backs the parent body away from the newborn on its wheels, 550 mm back and 200 mm to port, the head dragged on the tank floor (4.2 N on the floor, about 1.3 N of friction at 0.3, estimate).

Tilt release: a cord round the tail face tilts each of the nine magnets on its hinged tab about its upper edge, so the magnets peel off the steel disks of the cuff (12.8 N each against 39 N of cord, not a straight pull); then the tail backs off 60 mm. The old head stays, empty of its next head, its gel still in its lobe.
The tail moves to the starboard lane.
The tail drives forward in the lane past the old head.
Behind the newborn, the tail moves onto its axis. The newborn has not moved: it lies where it came to rest.
The tail docks on the rim of the newborn: the cuff magnets of the tail meet the steel disks in the cuff of the newborn.

Gel: 4.37 L from the gel bottle outside the tank, through the port in the tail and the line on the arm, at 0.1 L a minute (44 minutes), into the lobe of the newborn; with the 1.02 L the tail still holds this is the 5.39 L every cycle starts with. The old head keeps its own 4.39 L as ballast.
Lip circuit: the channels of the lower lip of the newborn are filled with gel at 9 kPa through the same line, 0.11 L (the gap between the skins over the lip circuit, less skins and webs).
The next cycle begins with the newborn as head. A new pair of tile sets is needed: the tail held one pair (one birth per refill).

checks.name: Tail in two prints, each one piece on the H2S: front (docking face, arm, saddles, kit magazine) 247 x 314 x 336 mm, rear (the store and the taper, with the sleeve of the joint) 230 x 220 x 316 mm, of 340 x 320 x 340
Everything for the tools is behind the docking plane: the saddles, the two modules and the kit store end 4 mm behind the plane. Only the stems and the kit stand in the gel, which runs across the seam

No tool crosses a wall: close to its base the arm holds the needle tip at most 18 mm high (at 150 mm from the axis), so the print needle and the holder hang with their stems in the gel and travel in the gel to the print; a wall at the docking plane could be only 17 mm tall
Folded arm ends 50 mm behind the docking plane; tower top 11 mm under the tail roof
The print needle reaches all 721 sampled print points inside the official joint ranges

The soft strip passes the mouth cupped: 194 mm wide and 26.4 mm thick (6 layers), laid on the true mouth contour as an arc of radius 90 mm (at least 3 times the thickness, 79 mm), resting on the lip, it clears the rim offset by half its thickness plus 2 mm by 3.5 mm more (calc/cup.py). As a flat box it would be 48 mm too wide (note only)

Keel, fed first: two rows of tubes 16 mm across (32 mm wide band) along the floor centerline, Dragon Skin 30 at 22.9 kPa (allowed 25.4): axial capacity p A 9.2 N against twice the largest push, 5.6 N; thrust 9.2 N against 2.2 N of gel drag on a turning panel; past the lip edge it bridges about 28 mm before it bends down onto the water

Reach: the holder pushes the rim to x = 292 mm (ball needle in the valve, official joint ranges); the folding crank (120 mm forward of the tool axis, hinged 30 mm down the stem, a 15 mm needle at its end) takes the rim to x = 391 mm at most; needed 386 mm (20 mm past the lip); 0 poses out of reach on the timeline

A rigid crank cannot park: its needle would stand at least 245 mm from the arm base. So the crank is on the holder and folds up along the stem, held by an over center torsion spring (preload 0.010 N m, rate 0.0064 N m per radian, against the crank moment of about 0.005 N m: margin 2). No motor: before the birth the arm presses the crank tab against a fixed stop on the holder saddle, the crank passes the center and the same spring holds it down; pressing it against the stop the other way folds it again

Pay out (round 5, calc/partD.py): the strip leaves the stack along its own length, the folds travel along it and no panel turns in the gel; the keel bends the layers through the traveling fold with margin 2.2. The arm alone pushes (the keel pressure pushes the front end forward and the rim backward into the needle: no net thrust): 2.6 N for the traveling fold plus 25 Pa shear on both faces of the strip in the gel; the pay out starts with at most 123 mm of strip in the gel for a margin of 1.3 on the 4.9 N payload (1.09 with 200 mm)
checks.value: phase a starts with the front panel at the lip

checks.name: Push per phase (only the part on the lower line above the gel, 49 mm from where it leaves the gel to the edge, weighs in air; behind it the gel drags at 25 Pa on both faces): a 2.80 N, b 2.59 N, c 1.32 N; the needle stays under the payload of 4.9 N, margin 1.75. Wrist moment 0.28 N m with the ball needle, 0.13 N m with the crank (push times the lever from the needle up to the wrist)

Inflation front kept outside: the six serpentines are fed from the mouth end in metered steps, 8 mL of air per mm of advance, 1.0 L per minute at 2 mm per second (the inflator gives 7.1); the front stays 15 mm past the lip edge, cells inside stay collapsed because the serpentine reaches them last
The rim zone fills last, outside: open, the rim is 316 mm wide against a mouth of 213 mm, so it would lock in the mouth if it filled earlier

Phase d, rear on the lip edge through the keel, front on the tank floor: 3.99 N on the lip edge. No deep lip cells (round 3): the lip beyond the top of the S is a 36 mm cantilever of the ordinary 18 mm channels, which run along it. At the quilt pressure (6.31 kPa) it would use 102 percent of its wrinkling moment (x 2 on the load); its circuit is filled with gel at 9.0 kPa (allowed 9.5 in these cells), which raises the tension and so the wrinkling moment 1.43 times: 76 percent
checks.value: lip circuit gel at 9 kPa: bench test

checks.name: The lip edge dips 3.9 mm under the keel (cantilever of the skins, no pressure stiffening: an upper bound), shown in phase d; the print has left the gel then, which stands at 80 mm, 20.1 mm under the dipped edge (with the print in it would be 0.6 mm)

The gel surface stays under the lip edge at every moment with the print in: it is highest (100 mm) with the whole folded print in it, the gel volume being set for that; the lip edge stands 4.5 mm higher (it dips 3.9 mm only in phase d, when the print is out), so 346 mL more would have to enter the gel (surface 0.077 m2) to reach it; in the birth the opened newborn keeps its cells inside the head collapsed (metered feed), so it displaces no more than the pack did

Float: the free newborn does not float: it weighs 15.6 N, the air in its lower cells (its lip circuit still empty) carries all but 10.7 N, which rest on the tank floor; it lies level in front of the mouth and does not swim off by itself

The gel has its place: the lower part of the head (the lobe, now 224 mm wide, simple version 96) holds 5.39 L with the folded next head in (simple version 2.85 L); the gel stands at 100 mm, 4.5 mm under the lip

Water level with the gel without the print: 80.5 mm (simple version 88.5 mm). With the print in, the gel stands 20 mm higher than the water, 193 Pa at the floor on the soft lobe walls; spanning floor to shelf they use 17 percent of their wrinkling moment (x 2 on the load); as a cantilever from the floor 45 percent

Flow channels (round 3, point E): long seams from the docking rim to the mouth along the form, up the S curve into the lip, channels 18 mm wide, 208 channel segments; the quilt 14.8 mm thick at most on the flanks and roof (round 2: 34.5), shallower toward both rims (webs as for 11 mm channels, 9 mm). Every fold line along the body (the 3 across folds of the pack) is a seam; cross seams every third of the length, staggered: on the even channels they lie on the two fold lines across the body, the odd channels are crossed there at right angles. Six serpentine circuits (lobe, flank and roof, each side), filled from the mouth end; 91 percent of the steps go to a neighboring segment, 18 need a short passage

Dragon Skin 10 NV first: the section above the gel as a two hinged arch on the lobe needs 3.07 kPa (loads x 2), the largest bulge of its cells allows 3.00 kPa (limit point / 1.5). Nine variants of cell size and bulge tried, none passes

Dragon Skin 30 (Dragon Skin 20 would carry the arches, allowed 5.44 kPa, but its 18 mm lip channels allow only 5.4 kPa, under the 9 kPa of the lip circuit): needs 3.07 kPa, allows 9.54 kPa; working pressure 6.31 kPa, margin 2.05 on the need and 1.51 on the allowed value; skins 1.2 mm, webs 0.8 mm; the cells 11 to 15 mm deep, no gel ballast in the cells
checks.value: Dragon Skin 30 printed in Carbopol is a bench test

checks.name: Lower lip, its own weight as a quilted cantilever of 36 mm: 4 percent of its wrinkling moment

Flat pack (laid flat, Z folded 3 across and 3 along, 18 layers of 4.4 mm): 123 x 194 x 79 mm, packing 0.62; the needle serves it from x = 117 mm, 5.7 mm clear of the chin, 15 mm clear of the lobe walls, 17 mm of gel over it
checks.value: 1 mm gel gaps as in the doublewall gates; the simple build kept 2 mm

checks.name: Enlarged lower shell, the form kept: lobe 224 mm wide (simple 96), gel 5.39 L (simple 2.85 L); spindle, roof arc, mouth and lower lip unchanged

Printed full of gel: 0.33 L in the 1 mm gaps. Clearing it inside the parent through a collapsed channel needs 103 kPa (2 tau L / h, 25 Pa, 2.1 m); in the open cells outside, a plug through 4 mm passages 11 to 32 kPa (9 to 25 Pa). Both above the 6.3 kPa of the quilt: the gel stays, as a film and as ballast in the lobe
checks.value: kept, counted as load above the water (0.5 mm film, estimate)

checks.name: Quilted rim on the tail face: nine pairs of DC2-N52 in the face and 18 x 3 mm steel disks in a solid cuff (doublewall gates G4), about 121 N; the air nipple on the face seats in the valve block of the cuff and feeds the six circuits through a relief valve at 6.3 kPa; tilt release 12.8 N per magnet against 39 N of cord (G7)
Tail alone in 80.5 mm of water with its gel, store empty: 8.8 N on the floor; with 1.2 kg of steel under the arm base (allowed for the tail) 19.1 N for the wheels of the relay
Quilted head alone with its gel at the water level: 5.81 kg against 5.38 kg of buoyancy (the air in the lobe cells under the water lifts 0.62 kg): 4.2 N on the floor

Relay and next cycle (round 6): the tail backs the parent body 550 mm back and 200 mm to port, tilt releases the old head, goes round it in the starboard lane, docks on the rim of the newborn where it rests, fills it with 4.37 L of gel from the bottle through its line (44 minutes; with the 1.02 L the tail kept, the 5.39 L of every cycle) and its lip circuit at 9 kPa (0.11 L, from the geometry of the lip channels); the next cycle begins with the newborn as head, a new pair of tile sets needed. Least clearance of the tail to the old head and the newborn 10.9 mm, of the tail and the old head to the tank walls 31.9 mm (tank made to order, inner 2110 x 800 mm)
checks.value: wheels and tilt release: bench test

checks.name: The first head is a quilted head too, cast or printed in a gel bath outside the tank beforehand; the H2S prints only the tail (two prints) and the molds
Per frame penetration test over 3102 frames (arm, tools, kit, the folded next head as it is printed, the inner skin of the head, the rack, the store): deepest overlap of any pair 0.67 mm (limit 1 mm)

The stiff parts lie in the interlayer on cast tiles (Dragon Skin 30, 1.2 mm, 6 mm lap), on the floor of the lobe beside the keel band, 27 to 63 mm from the rim, long axes along the body: the Bartels mp6 piezo micropump (30 x 15 x 3.8 mm, 2 g) with its mp-Lowdriver (25.6 x 10.3 x 5.0 mm), the LiPo 1578 (36 x 29 x 4.75 mm) and the controller, side by side. They lift the 17 layers above them in the pack by at most 4.0 mm: the stack top 87.2 mm, 12.8 mm under the gel. Pockets with tile and cover skin: mp6 6.2, driver 7.4, LiPo 7.2, controller 5.6 mm, all within the 10 mm target. The quilt where they lie is the flat double skin of the lobe floor, 2.5 to 3.0 mm (derive.py), so every pocket swells the floor by a few mm

Controller (round 7): the CodeCell C6 Drive (9.4 mm, product page) made an 11.8 mm pocket, over the 10 mm target, and no quilt of 12 mm lies on the floor where the parts must go (the floor quilt is 2.5 to 3.0 mm). Chosen instead: an Espressif ESP32-C3-MINI-1 module (13.2 x 16.6 x 2.4 mm, datasheet) on a 0.8 mm carrier with the LiPo charger and a regulator, 3.2 mm, a 5.6 mm pocket. Its radio works only near the surface: 2.4 GHz does not pass far through water

Water: the mp6 moves 6 to 12 mL of water a minute (typ. 8, datasheet, at 250 Vpp; the mp-Lowdriver gives at most 150 Vpp, so less), against up to 600 mbar: a trim and signal pump (a visible thread of water at the outlet port under the floor, a slow ballast shift between channels), not propulsion. The newborn does not move by itself

The tiles reach the gel before the print by the verified kit motion, in two trips of the holder (set 1: the mp6 and its driver; set 2: the LiPo and the controller, each at most 57 mm across, what the pick pocket allows); the tail carries one pair of sets per birth: one birth per refill (a limit)

verdict.point: Q1 the birth through the mouth, without clipping
verdict.why: Keel first, mouth end first: the keel (two rows of 16 mm tubes at 23 kPa) opens the folds and carries the push; the strip passes the mouth cupped (radius 90 mm); the holder pushes the rim to x 292 mm, its folding crank to 386 mm, 20 mm past the lip; the rim zone fills last, outside. Deepest overlap over the birth 0.54 mm.

verdict.point: Q2 the gel has its place
verdict.why: The lower part of the head holds 5.39 L at 100 mm; the water stands at the gel level without the print (80.5 mm). The lobe walls are held by their own quilt at 6.3 kPa, the water outside at nearly the same level and the floor; with the print in the gel stands 20 mm over the water (193 Pa), within the walls (estimate).

verdict.ok: yes in Dragon Skin 30, no in 10 NV
verdict.why: 208 cells, 14 to 42 mm, irregular, turning; six serpentine circuits. Dragon Skin 10 NV fails (3.07 kPa needed, 3.00 allowed); Dragon Skin 30 at 6.31 kPa (needs 3.07, allows 9.54).
Flat pack 3 x 3, 123 x 194 x 79 mm, in the enlarged lobe (224 mm wide); every point in the reach of the needle; printed on the timeline.
0.33 L printed in the gaps; clearing needs far more than the quilt pressure inside or outside; it stays as a film and as ballast in the lobe.

Nine magnet pairs and steel disks in the cuff, nipple and relief valve, tilt release, 1.2 kg of steel in the tail. The relay runs in the tank made to order (inner 2110 x 800 mm): least clearance 10.9 mm to the heads, 31.9 mm to the glass; the newborn gets 4.37 L of gel and 0.11 L in its lip circuit.

cast outside the tank in a two part mold of the head form (the H2S prints the mold halves and a core for each skin layer), or printed in a gel bath outside beforehand by the same arm on a bench; the H2S prints only the tail (two prints) and the molds.

limits: The birth (round 2) is a kinematic model checked against the colliders: the strip is drawn as six layers laid on the keel and cupped, each section opens across within 35 mm past the lip, the opened part follows the keel down to the floor. Not modeled: the flow in the cells, wrinkles, the gel film moving inside the cells, friction in detail. The crank is held by a passive over center latch (bench test). The relay is a kinematic model on wheels (no wheel slip, no drag of the water on the bodies).

The quilt is sized as a 2D two hinged arch per section (loads x 2, the ballooning limit of the largest bulge / 1.5, wrinkling of the skin on the compression side); the shell action along the body is not counted. The cells are drawn with their webs and bulges as computed, the seams as lines.

Bench tests: (1) Dragon Skin 30 printed in Carbopol in 1 mm gaps; (2) a quilted section at 6.3 kPa, crown drop and wrinkling; (3) folding at the seams, 18 layers; (4) the soft lobe walls with the gel 20 mm over the water; (5) gel film left in the cells; (6) the tilt release of the cuff magnets; (7) the open gel face at the water level.
Estimates: the yield stress of the gel (25 Pa), friction 0.3, the gel film left in the cells (0.5 mm), the magnet pull through the cuff, the passages between cells (4 mm).
Overlap is measured from sampled points against exact surfaces; the folded next head is tested as its box against the arm and its points against the inner face.

read.tank_text: The tank is made to order, 2140 x 830 x 600 mm outside, 15 mm low iron glass, inner 2110 x 800 mm (the relay lane needs 0.76 m across). The water stands 83 mm deep (the gel level without the print): 129 L with the parent body docked in it (129 kg). Glass about 196 kg (2500 kg per cubic meter, estimate), the parent body 14.0 kg: about 338 kg filled, 1.9 kPa on the floor under it.

attempts.name: Push the pack as one block, as the doublewall build pushed its flat pack
attempts.why: The pack (123 x 194 x 79 mm) does not pass the mouth as a block (48 mm short of the opening at its tightest height). Even narrower, it would have to leave the gel and climb onto the lower lip, which stands 4.5 mm above the gel and 24.0 mm above the water: on the lip the whole newborn (1.59 kg) is in air, 15.6 N against the DexArm payload of 4.9 N, and the friction alone (0.3) is 4.7 N. And at the height of the lip the holder reaches x = 274 mm, so the rear of the pack stays 92 mm inside the mouth.

attempts.name: Unfold the pack in the gel and feed the strip out flat over the lip, the arm pushing hand over hand at bosses; the last part freed by the parent body backing away
attempts.why: A flat strip folded 7 across (83 mm wide, 62 mm thick) is the least folded strip that passes the mouth on the lip (8 mm to spare; folded 6 across it would clear the rim by only 0.9 mm, under the 2 mm kept). Pushed flat over the lip it does not buckle, and the push is about 1.0 N (friction on the lip in air 0.5 N, gel drag 0.5 N at 25 Pa), under the payload. The last 92 mm beyond the reach of the holder could come from the parent body backing away on the drive of the relay while the opened part outside rests on the floor (anchor about 2.6 N). But that strip does not fit the print room: folded 2 along the pack is 175 mm long where the needle serves 93 mm; folded 3 along it stands 185 mm tall where the gel allows 93 mm. With 1.0 mm skins and 0.8 mm gaps it would still be 175 mm long (2 along) or 151 mm tall (3 along).

attempts.name: Push the strip partly inflated, so that it carries the push like a beam and can be pushed past the reach
attempts.why: Inflated, each of the 14 layers of the strip folded 7 across is 14 mm deep (median cell): the strip becomes 204 mm thick and 83 mm wide, 53 mm more than the mouth gives at the heights it must pass. Inflating only some layers leaves the others to buckle. And the interlayer air does not drive the body forward: it fills cells, it does not lengthen the body, and the trailing rim is the widest section of the newborn, so the last 92 mm still stay beyond the reach.

needs: a reach of the holder to about x = 396 mm at the height of the lip (now 274): 122 mm more, for example the DexArm on a slide, which the simple version removed
or a lower lip at the water level and within the reach, which is the shorter head with the mouth open to the floor of the doublewall build, excluded by the brief

or a newborn closed for the birth (thin membranes across the rim and the mouth, cut after the birth), so that its lumen can be inflated and the body grows through the mouth as in the simple version; but the trailing rim is the widest section (1163 mm of perimeter against 664 mm of mouth rim), so it would have to fold in the mouth with nothing to drive it

q6.nipple: short spout on the tail face, seated in the valve block of the cuff low on the port side; feeds all six circuits through a relief valve at 6.3 kPa

q7.how: cast outside the tank in a two part mold of the head form (the H2S prints the mold halves and a core for each skin layer), or printed in a gel bath outside beforehand by the same arm on a bench; the H2S prints only the tail (two prints) and the molds
